bigpic.b: Wall Street shrugged off a steep morning rout
bigpic.t: as the Dow erased a 1,105-point drop to close higher, though Nvidia still fell 3.9% on renewed AI doubts.

bigpic.b: Washington proposed new tariffs on 14 economies
bigpic.t: including up to 20% on Singapore and 18% on Malaysia, with final decisions unlikely before late January.
after the Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, while hot US inflation kept a December Fed hike near certain.

stories.h: Wall Street claws back a steep morning slide as the Dow ends 164 points higher
stories.sum: The Dow erased a drop of about 1,105 points to close up 0.33% at 50,182.95, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.25% to 7,182.78 after falling as much as 3.2%. The Nasdaq ended 0.62% lower at 23,585.80, having been down about 4.6%. US markets are shut for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday.
stories.why: The wild intraday swing shows how fragile sentiment is, with AI stocks, hot inflation and new tariffs all weighing at once.

stories.h: US PCE inflation hits 3.8% in October as third-quarter growth is revised up to 4.3%
stories.sum: The Fed's preferred price gauge rose 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, while core prices climbed 3.3%, a tenth above forecasts. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised to an annualised 4.3% from 3.4%. Consumer spending was flat after inflation and the saving rate stood at 4.1%.
stories.why: Hot prices alongside strong growth make a Fed hike on 9 December near certain, pushing borrowing costs higher across the economy.

stories.h: Kospi closes down 6.2% at its lowest since January as Asia's chip rout deepens
stories.sum: The Kospi fell 6.16% to 4,697.51, its lowest close since 13 January, as foreign investors dumped a net 1.95 trillion won of shares. Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 2.8% to 57,011.62, Taiwan's Taiex about 5% and the Shanghai Composite 1.5% to its lowest in more than a year. Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped 0.3%.
stories.why: Asian indices are packed with chip makers, so doubts about AI demand are now dragging on the whole region's markets.

stories.h: Nvidia sinks 3.9% as the rally on Jensen Huang's return fades and chip stocks swing
stories.sum: Nvidia closed at $149.30 after falling more than 8% early, giving back part of Monday's roughly 30% jump on Huang's return as chief executive. Oracle fell about 5% and Micron about 4.5%, and Ambarella lost 19.8% on weak guidance tied to memory costs. The Philadelphia chip index ended down 0.65% after a 7% morning slide.
stories.why: Violent swings in AI leaders show investors doubting whether chip demand and spending can justify their valuations.

stories.h: Anthropic recovers from an early 9% drop as Wall Street analysts start coverage
stories.sum: Anthropic shares touched $75.71 in early trade before closing up 1.08% at $82.79, just under the $83 IPO price. Arete started coverage at buy with a $300 target, Oppenheimer at outperform with $150 and Canaccord at buy with $135, while ARK Invest bought shares across its funds on Tuesday.
stories.why: Bullish first research calls could steady the biggest AI listing after a rocky start that has unsettled the IPO market.

stories.h: Samsung and SK hynix plunge as brokers call an early peak in the memory boom
stories.sum: SK hynix fell 11.05% and Samsung Electronics 9.87%, pushing Samsung's value below 1,000 trillion won for the first time since March. BNP Paribas cut its Micron target to $775 from $1,700, and TrendForce trimmed its fourth-quarter NAND price forecast. Dell's operations chief said he still expects memory prices to rise.
stories.why: Memory makers have led the AI rally, so an earlier pricing downturn would hit earnings across the chip supply chain.

stories.h: Fed's Beige Book finds modest growth, firmer wage gains and stubborn cost pressures
stories.sum: Eight of the Fed's 12 districts reported slight to moderate growth and four saw no change, with prices and wages both rising moderately and wage gains picking up from the last report. The Atlanta Fed said banks stayed cautious as consumer lending grew and more shoppers used buy now, pay later for groceries and meals.
stories.why: Firmer wages give policymakers another reason to raise rates on 9 December, keeping funding costs high for lenders and borrowers.

stories.h: Treasury yields slip as investors seek safety, with a December Fed hike still priced in
stories.sum: The 10-year Treasury yield ended near 4.85%, down about 6 basis points, after dipping to 4.83% as tech shares slid in the morning. CME FedWatch showed about 97% odds of a quarter-point Fed hike on 9 December. US bond markets are closed for Thanksgiving and shut early on Friday.
stories.why: Lower long yields ease mortgage and corporate borrowing slightly, but a near-certain hike keeps short-term funding expensive for banks.

stories.h: Bank of Korea decides at 9am Singapore time, with a hike to 3.25% widely expected
stories.sum: The central bank's final decision of 2026 is due at about 10am in Seoul, along with new economic forecasts. A Reuters poll found 32 of 34 economists expect a quarter-point rise from 3%, with inflation at 2.8% in October, and most see a final hike to 3.5% early next year. It comes a day after the Kospi's 6.2% slump.
stories.why: A hike during a stock rout would raise Korean borrowing costs and show the central bank putting inflation ahead of market stress.

stories.h: Bitcoin climbs back above $60,000 as November ETF outflows near a record $5B
stories.sum: Bitcoin traded around $60,140 on Wednesday evening in New York, up about 0.7% on the day, after dipping to about $58,500 early as tech stocks tumbled. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost a record $4.94B in November through 24 Nov, with BlackRock's IBIT taking 84% of withdrawals. Bitcoin is still down more than 20% this month.
stories.why: Steady institutional selling has removed the main buyer behind bitcoin's rally, leaving prices exposed to swings in leveraged trading.

stories.h: Fidelity files for a spot Chainlink ETF to trade on Nasdaq
stories.sum: Fidelity filed with the SEC on 25 Nov for the Fidelity Chainlink Fund, to list on Nasdaq under the ticker FLNK. The fund would hold LINK tokens directly and would not stake them. It would compete with Grayscale's and Bitwise's Chainlink funds, which held about $112M and $42M respectively as of 24 Nov.
stories.why: Big asset managers keep widening crypto ETF menus beyond bitcoin and ether, even as investors pull money from the sector.

stories.h: Stablecoin supply shrinks by more than $21B in six weeks as cash leaves crypto
stories.sum: Dollar stablecoins in circulation fell to about $282.4B on 25 Nov from $304B on 14 Oct, DefiLlama data show. Kaiko counted about $12B of net redemptions across 11 tokens in the 30 days to 13 Nov, with Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC each down about 4%, mostly on Ethereum.
stories.why: Shrinking balances signal less cash parked for crypto trading, though on-chain payment volumes in the tokens have kept growing.

stories.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41B in pharma's biggest deal since 2023
stories.sum: Sanofi will pay $175 a share in cash, a 46% premium to Insmed's 18 Nov price. It gains Brinsupri for bronchiectasis, with $1.09B of sales in the first nine months, plus Arikayce and the Phase 3 lung drug TPIP. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027. Insmed rose about 14% early, and Sanofi closed up 9.8% in Paris.
stories.why: Gives Sanofi new respiratory growth before Dupixent, about 40% of group revenue, loses its main US patent in 2031.

stories.h: FDA approves Cogent's bezuclastinib combination for advanced GIST
stories.sum: The FDA cleared Cogent Biosciences' Ekitna (bezuclastinib) with Pfizer's older drug sunitinib for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours previously treated with imatinib. In the Phase 3 PEAK trial, the combination held off disease progression for a median 16.5 months, against 9.2 months on sunitinib alone.
stories.why: Adds a new later-line option in a rare cancer and lifts the commercial prospects of a mid-sized oncology biotech.

stories.h: AbbVie's Rinvoq wins US approval as the first systemic treatment for vitiligo
stories.sum: The FDA approved upadacitinib on 23 Nov for nonsegmental vitiligo in patients aged 12 and older, making it the first systemic therapy cleared in the US for the skin condition. BridgeBio also won full approval the same day for Welgemda in a rare form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
stories.why: Widens Rinvoq's reach in skin disease as AbbVie leans on newer immunology drugs to replace lost Humira sales.

stories.h: Brent jumps 3.5% to $94.61 after Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura
stories.sum: The Houthis said they hit Ras Tanura, the kingdom's largest refinery, and Riyadh's financial district on 25 Nov. The Saudi-led coalition said air defences downed four drones over the site and reported no damage, and Bloomberg found no disruption to output or exports. Brent settled up $3.21, and WTI rose 2% to $83.68.
stories.why: Repeated attacks on Gulf energy sites keep a risk premium in oil even as forecasters expect a supply surplus.

stories.h: OPEC+ meets Sunday on 2027 quotas as Iraq disputes its capacity estimate
stories.sum: Ministers meet on 29 Nov to set 2027 output using the group's first capacity review. Iraq, given a preliminary capacity of 4.9M barrels a day, wants a higher figure and has warned it could leave if its quota is not raised, and Kazakhstan is also pushing back. Russia's Alexander Novak says the review should finish by year-end.
stories.why: The quota split decides which producers can pump more in 2027 as the market tips toward surplus.

stories.h: US tells Americans to leave Iran immediately, warning hostilities could escalate
stories.sum: A security alert from the US Virtual Embassy in Iran told citizens not to travel there for any reason and to leave at once, warning that Iran, the Houthis and allied groups may target US companies and institutions. It follows Iranian attacks on US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait and a Houthi strike that wounded 11 people in Riyadh.
stories.why: An evacuation call signals Washington is bracing for escalation that could threaten Gulf energy sites and tanker routes.

stories.h: China's car sales slump 27% in October, setting off a wave of discounts
stories.sum: Passenger car retail sales fell 27.1% from a year earlier to 1.643M in October, and new-energy vehicle sales dropped 13.7% to 1.109M, Gasgoo data show. Sales in the first half of November were down 25%. At least 10 carmakers have signalled price cuts, and Tesla on 24 Nov extended cheaper Model 3 financing to 31 Dec.
stories.why: A sharp demand slump deepens China's price war, squeezing margins for local brands and foreign rivals alike.

stories.h: Canada's Detroit carmakers call Ottawa's Chinese EV quota a 'Trojan horse'
stories.sum: Canada's deal with China lets in 49,000 Chinese-made EVs this fiscal year at a 6.1% tariff instead of 100%, rising to 70,000 by 2030. The Canadian Vehicle Manufacturers' Association, which represents Ford, GM and Stellantis, wants the pact scrapped, saying the quota equals 30% of 2025 EV sales. Tesla has used most of it so far.
stories.why: Opening Canada to cheaper Chinese EVs would sharpen price competition for Detroit carmakers in one of their core markets.

stories.h: BYD enters exclusive talks to buy Ineos' Hambach car plant in France
stories.sum: BYD said it is in exclusive negotiations to buy the Hambach factory in Moselle, near the German border, which Ineos Automotive has owned since 2020 and uses to build its Grenadier 4x4. The deal depends on consultation with staff representatives. President Macron and Industry Minister Sebastien Martin welcomed the plan.
stories.why: Building cars inside the EU would cut BYD's exposure to tariffs on China-made EVs and speed its push into Europe.

stories.h: Poundland falls into administration, putting about 11,000 jobs at risk
stories.sum: The UK discount chain appointed AlixPartners as administrators on 25 Nov after sale talks with bidders including Martin Property Group failed to find a solvent deal. Its roughly 600 stores keep trading while buyers are sought, and Tesco and B&M are reported to be interested in parts. Owner Gordon Brothers bought Poundland for £1 last year.
stories.why: A break-up would let rivals such as Tesco and B&M pick up sites, reshaping Britain's discount high street before Christmas.

stories.h: US online holiday spending tops $82.5B so far, up 9.1%, Adobe says
stories.sum: Shoppers spent more than $82.5B online from 1 to 22 Nov, and buy now, pay later spending rose 6.5% to $6.1B, Adobe Analytics data show. Adobe expects $6.9B on Thanksgiving, $12.9B on Black Friday and $15.1B on Cyber Monday. Visits to retail sites referred by AI assistants are up 127%.
stories.why: Solid online demand into the holiday peak supports retailers' fourth-quarter forecasts despite inflation running near 4%.

stories.h: Black Friday discounts run shallower than last year as retailers guard margins
stories.sum: Centric data cited by LSEG show the average US online discount at 30% this month, down from 33% in Black Friday week 2025, even as 38% of products are on sale against a 35% average last year. Specialty retailers' discounts shrank to 23% from 31%. LSEG expects fourth-quarter retail and restaurant earnings to rise 8.5% on 3.5% revenue growth.
stories.why: Shallower markdowns protect profits but test shoppers already stretched by inflation running at 3.7%.

stories.h: Hunger Games prequel heads for a Thanksgiving win as Hexed and Focker In-Law open
stories.sum: Lionsgate's Sunrise on the Reaping had taken $148.2M by Tuesday after a $119.3M debut, and Gold Derby sees it adding $78M over the five-day holiday. Disney's Hexed, which cost more than $200M, drew about $2M from Tuesday previews and is forecast at $40M, against $45M for Universal's poorly reviewed Focker In-Law.
stories.why: A soft start for Hexed would add pressure on Disney's costly original films just as the studio pushes to cut costs.

stories.h: Disney readies more cuts, with some managers told to find 20% savings
stories.sum: Disney has laid off more than 1,300 staff this year across HR, technology and TV, plus 8% of Marvel's workforce, and 159 parks roles go in December, the Los Angeles Business Journal reports. Bloomberg said some managers were asked to cut costs by 20%. The push comes despite fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rising 16% to about $26B.
stories.why: Even growing studios are trimming staff while shifting money into parks, cruise ships and technology, adding to Hollywood's job losses.

stories.h: Netflix buys Los Angeles' Radford Studio Center for $380M
stories.sum: Netflix bought the 55-acre Studio City lot, which has 22 stages, directly from Goldman Sachs-led lenders who took it from Hackman Capital Partners, which paid $1.85B in 2021. The streamer plans renovations and will keep the studio team, calling the purchase a meaningful new investment in California's film industry.
stories.why: Distressed studio lots are changing hands far below peak prices, letting streamers lock in production space cheaply.

stories.h: Airbus sells its US satellite-building unit to Cerberus to focus on autonomous aircraft
stories.sum: Cerberus Capital Management will buy the US space systems business of Airbus US Space & Defense, including its 200,000 sq ft Arrow satellite plant near Kennedy Space Center in Florida, with closing expected by year-end. Terms were not disclosed. Airbus says it will focus its US defence work on autonomous military aviation.
stories.why: Shows defence groups reshaping portfolios around uncrewed systems while private equity bets on demand for US-built satellites.

stories.h: Xiamen Airlines commits to 50 Boeing 737-8 jets, pending Beijing's approval
stories.sum: The China Southern unit agreed to take 50 737-8s worth about $7.4B at list prices, for delivery from 2031 to 2034. The deal still needs approval from China Southern's shareholders and the Chinese government. It came the same day as Malaysia Airlines' commitment for ten 787-10s.
stories.why: A firm Chinese narrowbody order would mark a step in Boeing's return to a key market where it lost ground during trade tensions.

stories.h: US Air Force orders 15 more Boeing KC-46 tankers for $2.82B
stories.sum: The contract change, awarded on 24 Nov for Lot 13, completes the initial 188-jet US tranche and lifts total KC-46A orders worldwide to 203. The tankers will be built in Seattle, with work due by June 2030. At about $188M each including services, Lot 13 costs more per jet than Lot 12's $165M.
stories.why: Steady tanker orders give Boeing's defence arm a long production runway as the Air Force replaces ageing KC-135s.

stories.h: US new home sales jump 14.2% in October despite 7% mortgage rates
stories.sum: Sales of new single-family homes rose to an annual rate of 701,000 in October from a downwardly revised 614,000 in September, Census data show, and were 7.5% higher than a year earlier. Supply fell to eight months, the lowest this year. Year-to-date sales remain 3% behind 2025, the National Association of Home Builders says.
stories.why: A surprise rebound offers builders some relief, though high rates keep resale activity near decade lows.

stories.h: US 30-year mortgage rate eases to 7.21% ahead of Thanksgiving
stories.sum: Freddie Mac's average 30-year fixed rate fell to 7.21% from 7.28% a week earlier, still well above 6.23% a year ago. The 15-year rate dropped to 6.54% from 6.66%. Freddie Mac's chief economist called the dip modest relief for prospective buyers heading into the holiday.
stories.why: Rates above 7% keep many buyers and sellers on the sidelines, limiting business for agents, lenders and builders.

stories.h: Beige Book says US housing weakened as affordability bit, with luxury holding up
stories.sum: Fed districts said home sales weakened as affordability hurt demand, commercial property was mixed and construction declined on high borrowing and building costs. Dallas reported a clear slowdown once mortgage rates passed 7%, with mid-priced homes softest, while Cleveland saw strength in luxury homebuilding and affordable housing.
stories.why: Points to a two-speed housing market in which mid-priced homes and their builders suffer most from high rates.

stories.h: US proposes tariffs of up to 20% on Singapore and 18% on Malaysia
stories.sum: USTR proposed duties on all goods from 14 economies on 25 Nov, ranging from 15% for the EU and Japan to 35% for Vietnam. Singapore's rate could drop to 10% with a trade deal, while Malaysia's could rise to 25% if talks fail. Chips and palm oil are exempt. Comments are due 5 Jan and hearings start 25 Jan.
stories.why: Singapore would face a higher rate than Japan or Korea, raising costs for exporters outside the chip exemption from early 2027.

stories.h: Singapore lifts its 2026 growth forecast to about 6% after a 6.1% third quarter
stories.sum: The economy grew 6.1% from a year earlier in the third quarter, beating the 5.4% advance estimate, as AI demand lifted electronics and machinery output. The trade ministry raised its 2026 forecast to around 6% from 4.5% to 5.5% and expects 2.5% to 4.5% growth in 2027. Non-oil domestic exports are now seen rising 30% to 32%.
stories.why: Booming AI-related exports give Singapore a cushion against new US tariffs but leave growth tied to one industry cycle.

stories.h: Anwar says the US is still Malaysia's top trade and investment partner
stories.sum: Speaking at Malaysia Aviation Group's Boeing order signing in Kuala Lumpur on 25 Nov, the prime minister warned against underestimating economic ties with Washington despite tariff disputes, and said Malaysia can deal with the US, China and Russia without taking sides. The FBM KLCI edged up 0.04% to 1,562.29 as regional markets fell.
stories.why: Signals Kuala Lumpur will keep negotiating rather than retaliating as Washington's new tariff proposal targets Malaysian goods.
